cohort: This study included all singleton births in the Medical Birth Registry of Norway from 1999 to 2022, comparing 134 births to mothers with MG to 1,351,032 non-MG births.
finding: Maternal MG increased the risk of elective C-section, induction, neuraxial anesthesia, episiotomy, preterm prelabor rupture of membranes, prolonged hospitalization, low birthweight, feeding problems, and transfer to a neonatal unit, with 4% of MG-exposed infants diagnosed with TNMG.
mod_finding: Elective C-section was twice as likely if the mother had MG, and the crude C-section rate was increased in preterm MG births and in MG births after previous C-section, suggesting a proactive management approach for MG deliveries.
